title: hpc
text: The hpc subcommand is used to configure HPC environments.

title: hpc
text:
Commands
  hpc       Master HPC setup
  hpc git
  hpc scratch
  hpc apptainer
  hpc slurm
  hpc r

title: hpc
text:
Installation
Assuming that the HPC is running on Linux, the following line will install setupmjr without requiring sudo permission:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr/main/install-local.sh | bash
Confirm that installation worked by running:
setupmjr --version
If the above does not work, then setupmjr may not be on your system PATH. In that case, you can add the following line to your shell profile (typically ~/.bashrc):
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
Then run:
source ~/.bashrc
At this point, the following should succeed:
setupmjr --version
If not, then the initial installation failed.

title: hpc
text:
Setup
The following command will configure the HPC environment:
setupmjr hpc
The master command is Linux-only and stops on the first failed setup step. It runs the following sequence:

Configure bash rc.d, executable paths, and login/profile integration.
Configure zsh rc.d, executable paths, and login/profile integration.
Configure Git and GitHub authentication.
Install the HPC scratch configuration.
Install the Apptainer helpers.
Install the SLURM helpers.
Configure R with the normal setupmjr r defaults.

In practical terms, setupmjr hpc does the following:

Helps store large files effectively: Large files are stored in the /scratch space (if available) rather than /home, to respect HPC storage policies.
Authenticates with Git: GitHub authentication uses either an existing persistent gh login or one protected setupmjr-managed token file for headless/HPC environments.
Adds Apptainer and SLURM helpers: If these tools are available, helper scripts are installed to simplify their usage.
Configures radian: If you use radian as your R terminal, it is configured to work properly on the HPC.

Each feature can also be configured independently via the respective subcommands (hpc scratch, hpc apptainer, hpc slurm, hpc git, hpc r).

Setting up Git
To configure Git, run:
setupmjr hpc git
This calls the normal setupmjr git setup. Authentication is deliberately suitable for headless HPC use:

if gh auth login has already established durable GitHub CLI authentication, Git is configured with gh auth setup-git;
otherwise setupmjr stores one GitHub token under ~/.config/setupmjr/auth/github.token, with private permissions, and configures Git to read it through the standard credential-helper interface.

The token itself is not embedded in shell startup files or Git configuration. Existing active GH_TOKEN= assignments left by older setupmjr versions are removed from setupmjr’s login.sh files during migration.
This credential-helper design is also intended to work with R gitcreds and with VS Code Dev Containers’ built-in Git credential forwarding. In a Remote SSH -> HPC -> Dev Container workflow, configure authentication on the HPC host first. If a particular Dev Container still fails to reuse the host helper, treat that as a forwarding problem rather than copying a PAT into the repository or container definition.
See git setup for the full authentication model and fallback details.


Using scratch space
HPCs typically have a separate scratch space for storing large files (i.e. /scratch/$USER), which is often faster and has different quotas than the home directory. The hpc scratch command helps you configure your environment to use the /scratch space effectively.
To set this up, run:
setupmjr hpc scratch
This configures the environment to preferentially use /scratch for:

Apptainer and Singularity images;
R libraries and renv caches.

title: hpc
text:
Details
The master setupmjr hpc command configures bash rc.d before installing ~/.bashrc.d/hpc-scratch.sh. The standalone hpc scratch subcommand only installs that file, so use setupmjr shell bash rc.d first if your shell is not already sourcing ~/.bashrc.d.

title: repo
text: The repo subcommand is used to set up repositories.

title: repo
text:
Commands
  repo readme
  repo devcontainer [--repo <owner>/<repo>@<branch>] [--build]
  repo action <action-name>
  repo install repos

title: repo
text:
repo readme
This command interacts with the user to scaffold a standardized README.md for a project repository.
When executed, it prompts for the following information: - The project title. - A brief description of what the repository does. - The full names and email addresses of two primary contacts.
It then generates a README.md using the provided inputs.

title: repo
text:
Details
The generated README.md follows a clean template containing sections for the title, purpose, contact details, links (e.g. data sources, publications), and further details (e.g. methods, timeline, team, data sources).
For example, the output might look like:
# My Project Title

This repository handles data processing for the survey data.

## Contact

For more information, please contact:
- Jane Doe:
  - jane.doe@example.com
- John Smith:
  - john.smith@example.com

## Links

- [URLs to data sources (e.g. OneDrive), GitHub repositories, publications, etc.]

## Details

[Methods, timeline, team, data sources, software/tools, etc.]

title: repo
text:
repo devcontainer
This command copies a reference .devcontainer configuration into your current repository.
setupmjr repo devcontainer [--repo <owner>/<repo>@<branch>] [--build]

--repo: Specifies the source repository and branch to copy the .devcontainer directory from (defaults to MiguelRodo/comp@main).
--build: If provided, the command will also download the relevant GitHub Action to automatically prebuild the devcontainer, fetching good default settings from the reference actions.

title: repo
text:
Details
Under the hood, the command downloads the specified branch tarball from GitHub over HTTPS and passes it directly to tar; repository and branch values are not interpolated into a shell command. If the --build flag is passed, it pulls the prebuild-devcontainer.yml workflow from MiguelRodo/actions and places it in .github/workflows/.

title: repo
text:
repo install repos
While setupmjr has a few subcommands like repo, the repos command is actually a dependency of setupmjr. The setupmjr repo install repos command downloads and installs this external repos utility into ~/.local/bin.
The core operations for managing repositories (cloning, configuring workspaces, etc.) are conceptually part of repos, which setupmjr uses or exposes.

title: repo
text:
repo action
This command simplifies adding pre-configured GitHub Actions to your repository.
setupmjr repo action <action-name>
It downloads the specified action workflow from the MiguelRodo/actions repository into your .github/workflows/ directory.

Available Actions
The following actions can be added:

prebuild-devcontainer: Builds and pushes a pre-built Dev Container image to GHCR whenever a SemVer tag is pushed. Read more here.
publish-quarto-site: Renders and publishes a Quarto site to the gh-pages branch whenever the main branch is updated. Read more here.
version-release: Bumps versions in Python or R packages, creates a versioned git tag, and publishes a GitHub Release. Read more here.

title: repo
text:
Details
When running repo action <action-name>, the CLI fetches the corresponding YAML file from the examples directory of the MiguelRodo/actions repository, directly placing it in .github/workflows/.

title: multirepo
text: The multirepo subcommand acts as a wrapper around the bundled repos utility, which is installed alongside setupmjr. It is designed to manage local workspaces and batch-process actions across multiple repositories.

title: multirepo
text:
Commands
  multirepo clone
  multirepo workspace
  multirepo codespace
  multirepo create
  multirepo <other repos command>
Any command passed to setupmjr multirepo will be automatically proxied to the bundled repos tool.

title: multirepo
text:
Details
The core operations for managing multiple repositories collectively (e.g. cloning a list of repositories, configuring cross-repo VS Code workspaces) are powered by the repos utility. The multirepo subcommand simplifies their execution from the setupmjr CLI.

title: Installation
text: setupmjr is distributed as a compiled Go CLI binary. Install it via system package managers, release installers, or from source. Optional R and Python wrappers dispatch to the installed setupmjr binary.

title: Installation
text:
Release asset matrix
GitHub Releases publish Go CLI binaries for:

Linux (amd64, arm64) as .tar.gz
macOS (amd64, arm64) as .tar.gz
Windows (amd64, arm64) as .zip (plus .exe bare binaries for installer scripts)
Stable direct-download bare binaries for installer scripts:

setupmjr_linux_<arch>
setupmjr_darwin_<arch>
setupmjr_windows_<arch>.exe


Python and R components are wrappers around the same CLI and are platform-neutral. Install the wrapper package (pip/R) and ensure setupmjr is installed on PATH.

title: Installation
text:
Ubuntu / Debian

Option 1: Local Release Installer (No sudo required)
Install the latest release binary into the first writable directory already present in your PATH:
git clone https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
cd setupmjr
bash install-local.sh
The installer also automatically downloads the repos tool as a bundled dependency. If no writable path entry exists, the installer will stop with guidance.
To uninstall:
bash uninstall-local.sh


Option 2: Install from APT Repository (Recommended for automatic updates, but requires sudo)






Warning



The APT repository is an upcoming feature and not yet fully configured.


Install and keep setupmjr up to date directly via apt:
# Install prerequisites
sudo apt-get install -y curl gpg

# Add repository signing key
curl -fsSL https://miguelrodo.github.io/apt-miguelrodo/KEY.gpg \
   | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/apt-miguelrodo.gpg

# Add apt source
echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/apt-miguelrodo.gpg] https://miguelrodo.github.io/apt-miguelrodo stable main" \
   | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/apt-miguelrodo.list >/dev/null

# Install setupmjr
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y setupmjr
To uninstall:
sudo apt-get remove setupmjr


Option 3: System-wide from Release .deb (requires sudo)
Prefer Option 1 (APT) for automatic updates. If needed, manually download and install a release .deb from the Releases page:
VERSION_SETUPMJR=1.2.6
ARCH="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"
wget "https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr/releases/download/v${VERSION_SETUPMJR}/setupmjr_${VERSION_SETUPMJR}_${ARCH}.deb"
sudo dpkg -i "setupmjr_${VERSION_SETUPMJR}_${ARCH}.deb"
rm "setupmjr_${VERSION_SETUPMJR}_${ARCH}.deb"

# Fix any dependency issues
sudo apt-get install -f
To uninstall:
sudo dpkg -r setupmjr

title: Installation
text:
macOS (Homebrew)






Warning



The Homebrew tap is an upcoming feature and not yet fully configured.


brew tap MiguelRodo/setupmjr
brew install setupmjr

title: Installation
text:
Windows

Option 1: Installer Script
Download and install the pre-compiled setupmjr.exe into the first writable directory already present in your PATH:

Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
cd setupmjr
Run the installer:
.\install.ps1

The installer downloads the latest setupmjr.exe binary from GitHub releases and places it in the first writable directory in your current PATH. It also automatically downloads the repos tool as a bundled dependency.
Requirements: PowerShell and network access to GitHub releases.
(Note: Ensure you are executing this within a PowerShell console pwsh or powershell.exe, as native cmd.exe will not interpret the script correctly.)
To uninstall:
.\install.ps1 -Uninstall


Option 2: Scoop
scoop bucket add setupmjr https://github.com/MiguelRodo/scoop-bucket
scoop install setupmjr

title: Installation
text:
From Source (Go)
Requires the Go toolchain installed.
Install directly from the remote module path:
go install github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr/cmd/setupmjr@latest
Or build from a local clone (Linux-specific example shown):
git clone [https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git)
cd setupmjr
go build -o setupmjr ./cmd/setupmjr
# Install system-wide on Linux/macOS
sudo mv setupmjr /usr/local/bin/

title: Installation
text:
Language Wrappers






Warning



The language wrappers are not created yet.



R Package
install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("MiguelRodo/setupmjr")
Requires setupmjr on your system PATH for full wrapper coverage.


Python Package
pip install git+https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
Or from a local clone:
git clone https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
cd setupmjr
pip install .
Requires setupmjr on your system PATH for full wrapper coverage.

title: Installation
text:
Verify Installation
setupmjr --help

title: shell
text: The shell subcommand is used to set up shell environments like bash or zsh. The bash subcommand acts as a shorthand for shell bash.

title: shell
text:
Commands
  shell <shell> rc.d
  shell <shell> path
  shell <shell> login

shell <shell> rc.d
To manage shell configuration more effectively, it is helpful to place individual scripts inside a dedicated directory (i.e. ~/.<shell>rc.d/) rather than cluttering the main ~/.<shell>rc file. The shell <shell> rc.d command sets up this directory and configures your ~/.<shell>rc to source all scripts inside it.
To set this up, run the following command:
setupmjr shell <shell> rc.d

title: shell
text:
Details
The shell <shell> rc.d command configures the environment by doing the following:

It ensures the ~/.<shell>rc.d directory exists.
It appends a loop to your ~/.<shell>rc to automatically source any readable scripts inside ~/.<shell>rc.d/:
for i in $HOME/.<shell>rc.d/*; do [ -r "$i" ] && source "$i"; done

title: shell
text:
Details
The shell <shell> path command ensures ~/bin and ~/.local/bin are accessible by doing the following:

It calls shell <shell> rc.d to ensure the ~/.<shell>rc.d/ directory is properly set up and sourced by ~/.<shell>rc.
It copies an embedded script, path-executables.sh, to ~/.<shell>rc.d/path-executables.sh. This script safely appends ~/bin and ~/.local/bin to the PATH environment variable if they are not already included.

Subcommands

hpc

title: project
text: Use the project command for shared project/operator tooling that is independent of agent configuration.

title: project
text:
Install or update pj
setupmjr project --pj
This installs pj from the canonical MiguelRodo/pj repository by shallow-cloning the floating v0 tag and running its installer. The v0 tag advances with compatible versioned pj releases, so this path follows the released v0 line rather than pj/main.
setupmjr does not own or vendor the pj implementation. It only installs the release selected by pj’s own floating release tag.

title: project
text:
Install the GitHub Projects skill
setupmjr project --gh-skill
This installs github-projects from MiguelRodo/github-projects-skill for universal agents at user scope. It is equivalent to:
gh skill install MiguelRodo/github-projects-skill github-projects --agent universal --scope user --force --pin main
The command installs the shared skill only. Repository-specific Project onboarding and .projects configuration remain separate concerns.
Both pieces may be installed or refreshed in one command:
setupmjr project --pj --gh-skill

title: r
text: The r subcommand is used to set up R environments.

title: r
text:
Commands
  r [--not-radian] [--not-lintr]

title: r
text:
Setup
One may often use a non-standard R terminal named radian because it offers many enhancements over the standard R terminal. However, radian (in some experiences) breaks without a key configuration setting.
To configure this setting, run the following command:
setupmjr r
In addition to configuring radian, this command also turns off object length and line linters for lintr (to prevent VS Code or other editors from bothering you because your variable names or lines are “too long”).

Flags
You can opt out of configuring radian or lintr by passing the respective flags:

--not-radian: Do not configure ~/.radian_profile.
--not-lintr: Do not configure ~/.lintr.

For example, to only configure radian and not lintr:
setupmjr r --not-lintr

title: r
text:
Details
If not skipped via --not-radian, the ~/.radian_profile file is created if it does not exist, and the following line is added to it:
options(radian.auto_match = FALSE)
If not skipped via --not-lintr, the ~/.lintr file is created if it does not exist, and the following lines are added to it:
linters: linters_with_defaults(
    object_length_linter = NULL,
    object_name_linter = NULL)

title: agent
text: Use the agent command for user-level coding-agent configuration. Provider setup belongs here; pj only launches already-configured agents.

title: agent
text:
Inspect agent configuration
Show the effective Codex provider, Copilot provider and configured opt-in subagent:
setupmjr agent --config
List the available choices and short aliases:
setupmjr agent --list
Running setupmjr agent without options prints command help.

title: agent
text:
Configure model-provider authentication
Store the DeepSeek API credential without changing any agent’s active provider:
setupmjr agent --auth deepseek
# short form
setupmjr agent -a d
The command reuses DEEPSEEK_API_KEY when it is already set, then checks the managed DeepSeek credential and existing Codex DeepSeek configurations. If no key is available, it prompts for one without echoing it.
The reusable key is stored at:
~/.config/setupmjr/agent/auth/deepseek.key
with private permissions. The credential can be reused by both the Codex and Copilot DeepSeek configurations.
Crucially, --auth is credential-only. It does not set COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE, COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL, COPILOT_MODEL, or any other provider-selection variable, and it does not change the current Codex or Copilot provider.
At present deepseek is the only managed --auth endpoint. The endpoint argument is explicit so additional credentials can be added without changing the command shape.

title: agent
text:
Switch the Copilot provider
GitHub-managed Copilot models are the default value for -p, so these are equivalent:
setupmjr agent -p
setupmjr agent -p g
setupmjr agent --copilot-provider github
Switch Copilot to DeepSeek:
setupmjr agent -p d
setupmjr agent --copilot-provider deepseek
DeepSeek provider selection requires the credential to have been stored first with:
setupmjr agent --auth deepseek
When DeepSeek is selected, setupmjr writes the managed Copilot environment at:
~/.config/setupmjr/agent/copilot.env
and sources it from Bash and Zsh startup files. The active DeepSeek configuration is:
COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic
COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic
COPILOT_MODEL=deepseek-flash
COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS=840000
COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=128000
Here, COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic selects the Anthropic-compatible wire protocol used to communicate with DeepSeek’s endpoint. It does not select Anthropic as the model vendor.
The raw DeepSeek key is not copied into the provider environment. The environment reads the private credential file only when DeepSeek is the active Copilot provider.
Switching back to github writes an environment that unsets the BYOK provider variables, restoring GitHub-managed Copilot model selection in new shells. Restart the shell, or source ~/.config/setupmjr/agent/copilot.env, after switching.
DeepSeek BYOK does not itself sign Copilot into GitHub. GitHub authentication remains separate and can coexist with either provider choice.

title: agent
text:
Switch the primary Codex provider
OpenAI/ChatGPT is the default value for -c, so these are equivalent:
setupmjr agent -c
setupmjr agent -c o
setupmjr agent --codex-provider openai
Switch Codex to DeepSeek:
setupmjr agent -c d
setupmjr agent --codex-provider deepseek
The first DeepSeek setup uses DeepSeek’s official Codex setup script and selects the Flash model. setupmjr reads DEEPSEEK_API_KEY when it is set, reuses a key from an existing managed DeepSeek configuration when possible, or prompts for the key without echoing it.
Before changing provider, setupmjr stores private snapshots of the active Codex config.toml and models.json under:
~/.config/setupmjr/agent/codex/
After both providers have been seen once, -c d and -c o switch by restoring those snapshots rather than rerunning the full DeepSeek installer.
If DeepSeek was already installed manually with the official setup script before setupmjr started managing providers, the first switch back to OpenAI uses DeepSeek’s official restore path once and then records the restored OpenAI state. Later switches are local snapshot restores.
Provider changes affect the ordinary Codex home at ~/.codex, so they apply to Codex clients that share that configuration. Restart active Codex clients after switching. A DeepSeek session may have logged Codex out of ChatGPT, so restoring the OpenAI configuration does not guarantee that the ChatGPT account is still authenticated.
The automated DeepSeek bootstrap currently requires Bash and curl, and is intended for Linux, macOS and WSL environments.

title: agent
text:
Configure an opt-in subagent
agy is the default value for -s:
setupmjr agent -s
setupmjr agent -s agy
setupmjr agent --subagent agy
This installs the bounded Codex guidance and narrow execution rule for delegating explicitly authorised work to Gemini through agy. Existing Codex instructions outside the managed block are preserved.
To use DeepSeek instead:
setupmjr agent -s deepseek
The DeepSeek subagent uses an isolated Codex home:
~/.codex-deepseek-subagent
It does not change the primary Codex provider. The managed guidance invokes the worker with codex exec --sandbox workspace-write and the isolated CODEX_HOME. As with agy, delegation remains opt-in: Codex may use the subagent only when you explicitly authorise it for the current task or conversation.
Selecting one subagent replaces the managed configuration for the other. --subagent-agy remains as a deprecated compatibility alias for --subagent agy.

title: agent
text:
Credential storage
setupmjr agent --auth deepseek stores the reusable DeepSeek API key in ~/.config/setupmjr/agent/auth/deepseek.key with private permissions. Authentication alone does not alter provider selection. When Copilot is explicitly switched to DeepSeek, its managed environment reads that file rather than embedding the raw key in .bashrc, .zshrc, or the provider environment.
DeepSeek’s official Codex format also stores the API key in config.toml. The saved DeepSeek provider snapshot therefore contains that key as well. setupmjr creates its provider-state directories with mode 0700 and writes credential and snapshot files with mode 0600. Treat these files as credentials and do not commit or share them.

title: git
text: The git subcommand configures Git identity and authentication.

title: git
text:
Commands
  git
  git profile
  git auth
  git auth text
  git auth cache
  git auth mngr

title: git
text:
Setting up Git
Run:
setupmjr git
This configures your Git name/email when they are missing and then configures GitHub authentication.
setupmjr git auth chooses between two durable authentication paths:

If gh has a persistent login for github.com, setupmjr runs gh auth setup-git --hostname github.com and lets GitHub CLI own the credential.
Otherwise, setupmjr uses its headless/HPC fallback and stores one token at ~/.config/setupmjr/auth/github.token.

The GitHub CLI check deliberately ignores GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN, so an environment-only token is not mistaken for a durable gh auth login.

GitHub CLI path
On a machine where GitHub CLI credential storage works well, authenticate once:
gh auth login
setupmjr git auth
The resulting Git credential helper is the standard GitHub CLI helper. Command-line Git and tools such as R gitcreds can consume the same Git credential interface.


Headless/HPC fallback
If no persistent gh login is available, setupmjr git auth reuses, in order:

GH_TOKEN;
GITHUB_TOKEN;
an existing ~/.config/setupmjr/auth/github.token;
otherwise a token entered at the prompt.

The token is stored once with private permissions: the auth directory is mode 0700 and github.token is mode 0600 on POSIX systems. The literal token value is not copied into .gitconfig, .bashrc, .zshrc, .bashrc.d/login.sh, or .zshrc.d/login.sh.
Git is configured with a host-specific credential helper that reads the protected token file only when Git requests a credential. For shell tools that consume GH_TOKEN, setupmjr places a small non-secret managed block in ~/.bashrc.d/login.sh and ~/.zshrc.d/login.sh; those files read the same protected token file when the shell starts. .bashrc and .zshrc only source their corresponding rc.d directories.
setupmjr git auth text explicitly selects this protected-token fallback. The text name is retained for backwards compatibility with the older command.


Migration from older setupmjr authentication
Older versions of setupmjr could write GH_TOKEN directly into .bashrc.d/login.sh and .zshrc.d/login.sh. Running the new authentication setup removes active legacy GH_TOKEN= and GITHUB_USERNAME= assignments from those setupmjr login files before configuring the new strategy.
A short-lived version of #53 also placed the non-secret managed block directly in .bashrc and .zshrc. Re-running setupmjr git auth migrates that block into the existing login.sh files automatically.


Dev Containers
VS Code Dev Containers supports Git credential-helper forwarding and copies Git configuration into the container. The preferred path is therefore to configure authentication once on the HPC host with setupmjr git auth and let Dev Containers reuse that Git credential helper.
The setupmjr fallback is deliberately implemented through the standard Git credential-helper interface for this reason. If a particular remote-HPC/container combination does not forward the helper correctly, test that environment before adding container-specific secret propagation. Do not bake a PAT into devcontainer.json, a Dockerfile, an image, or a repository file.


R gitcreds
gitcreds asks Git’s credential subsystem for credentials. Both setupmjr strategies configure that same subsystem, so gitcreds::gitcreds_get("https://github.com") can use the effective GitHub credential without a separate R-specific token store.

title: git
text:
Legacy explicit helpers
The older explicit helper commands remain available:
setupmjr git auth cache
setupmjr git auth mngr
They are not part of the default authentication path.
